subject: Access governance — runbook & handoff: SSO / SCIM / IP allowlist / service accounts
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Reed <claire.reed@medicore.com>, Thomas Li <thomas.li@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access governance — runbook & handoff: SSO / SCIM / IP allowlist / service accounts

Hi Claire / Thomas —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. As discussed, I attached a draft runbook that consolidates our SSO (SAML) configuration, SCIM attribute mappings, the IP allowlist plan, and the proposed service-account patterns for integration and automation. The goal for this thread: line up acceptance criteria and the first two-week implementation window so your infra team can validate before cutover.

High level ask for Medicore:
- Confirm public egress IP ranges you want on the allowlist for staging and prod (we need CIDR list and/or NAT gateway addresses).
- Confirm SCIM user attributes you plan to map (we included email, displayName, groups, and manager as a starting point).
- Approve the service-account role matrix in section 3 of the runbook (short-lived keys + least-privilege).

Attachments (stubs):
- medicore-access-runbook-v1.md (text/markdown, 9KB) — initial draft
- mutual-action-plan-20261027.pdf (application/pdf, 28KB) — timelines and owner map

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm IP ranges + SCIM attribute preferences by EOD Wed 10/28.
2) We schedule a 60-min implementation preflight (engineering + security) for Thu 10/29.
3) Dry-run in staging the week of 11/1; production cutover target 11/10 if dry-run is green.

If anything in the runbook is missing or unclear, flag it here and we’ll iterate.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: medicore-access-runbook-v1.md (text/markdown, 9KB)
From: Claire Reed <claire.reed@medicore.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Li <thomas.li@medicore.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:03:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access governance — runbook & handoff: SSO / SCIM / IP allowlist / service accounts

Thanks Jordan — this is clear and very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we commit to the timeline: 

1) IP allowlist: for staging we can provide the NAT gateway CIDRs (private cloud) but production will be behind our new egress proxy — team is finalizing the public IPs and hopes to have them by Thursday. Will that timeline work?

2) SCIM: we will *not* sync the manager field initially (we have a different HR mapping). Please remove manager from the required list; groups + email + displayName are fine for the first cut.

3) Service accounts: security wants a short write-up that justifies the two-role pattern (deploy vs monitoring) so they can sign off. Can you add a paragraph about least-privilege and rotation cadence?

We can do the preflight on Thu 10/29 at 10:00am PT. Thomas and I will be on the call; I’ll loop in Dave (infra) if we need ip-level network folks.

Claire Reed
Head of Platform Engineering | Medicore Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access governance — runbook & handoff: SSO / SCIM / IP allowlist / service accounts

Jordan / team — internal coordination notes and recommended plan (posting here before the preflight):

Summary of Claire asks:
- Accept staging NAT CIDRs now; production IPs expected Thu 10/29 (ok for timeline).
- Remove manager attribute from required SCIM mapping for v1.
- Add explicit justification paragraph for the two-role service-account pattern.

Recommended approach (two-phase):
Phase A — Preflight & Staging (week of 11/1)
- Deliverable: medicore-access-runbook-v2.md with updated SCIM fields + service-account justification paragraph.
- Action owners: Jordan (runbook update + preflight agenda), Monica (SCIM mapping template + test user export), Ben (billing/entitlements note on staging quotas).
- Validation: run SCIM sync to staging, verify group membership and provision/deprovision flow.

Phase B — Prod cutover (target 11/10)
- Deliverable: final runbook + signed MPA.
- Action owners: Claire (final IP list), Redwood infra (rotate test keys, finalize expiration/rotation cadence), Security (approve role matrix).

Blocked items and risks:
- Prod IPs delay could push cutover by >=1 week.
- If Medicore wants manager attribute later, that'll require HR mapping changes and an additional dry-run.

Let me know if you want the runbook updated before the preflight or if we just walk through changes on Thu call.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Reed <claire.reed@medicore.com>, Thomas Li <thomas.li@medicore.com>

Subject: Re: Access governance — runbook & handoff: SSO / SCIM / IP allowlist / service accounts

Claire / Thomas — attached is medicore-access-runbook-v2 with the updates we discussed:
- manager removed from required SCIM attributes; noted as v2 enhancement.
- Added a one-paragraph justification for the two-role service-account pattern (deploy vs monitoring) and recommended rotation cadence (30 days for deploy keys, 7 days for ephemeral automation tokens).
- Preliminary prod IP placeholder: 52.33.128.0/24 (this is a placeholder so your infra team has a test value; please replace with your final NAT/egress IPs).

Attachment (stub): medicore-access-runbook-v2.md (text/markdown, 12KB)

Preflight agenda (Thu 10/29, 10:00am PT):
- 10m: Introductions + acceptance criteria
- 20m: SAML config walk-through (IdP metadata, ACS URL, assertion attributes)
- 15m: SCIM test results and mapping validation (Monica)
- 10m: IP allowlist gating and NAT/egress specifics (Thomas / Dave if present)
- 5m: Rollout plan & next steps

If this looks good, I’ll update the MPA with the Phase A checklist and send an updated shared Drive link.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks, got the v2. 10:00am PT Thu works for us. Claire and I confirmed we’ll share final prod egress IPs by EOD Thu; if something slips we’ll let you know immediately.

Quick note: I’ll bring Dave from NetOps for the NAT discussion; he asked for the runbook section that lists the expected TCP ports (we included 443 already, but please confirm there are no additional ports needed for SCIM or health checks).

See you Thu — looking forward to the preflight.

Thomas Li
